explanation: This variant is not on erdosproblems.com/878 (which defines f(n) = Σ p_i^{ℓ_i} with n ∈ [p_i^{ℓ_i}, p_i^{ℓ_i+1})), so I compared it with the original paper [Er84e] (Erdős, 'On two unconventional number theoretic functions and on some related problems', scan at users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1984-16.pdf, p. 117): 'Denote max_{n≤x} ω(n) = h(x) = (1+o(1)) log x / log log x. Clearly m(x) < x h(x). ... I am sure that lim_{x→∞} (x h(x) − m(x))/x = ∞ (17). I could not prove (17) and (5)', with m(x) = max_{n≤x} f(n). In Lean, f n = Σ_{p ∈ primeFactors n} p^(Nat.log p n) (the largest power of p not exceeding n), m x = maxUpTo f x and h x = maxUpTo ω x are maxima over 0..x (the extra n = 0 contributes 0 to both), and the theorem states that ((x·h x − m x : ℕ) : ℝ)/x tends to +∞ along atTop. The natural-number subtraction is exact because f(n) ≤ ω(n)·n ≤ x·h(x) for n ≤ x, so no truncation occurs. The statement is exactly formula (17), in the affirmative form matching the 'solved' status and the linked Lean proof. Faithful.
